doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: Side jobs, work ethic and leaving private banking in 1985
summary: Vega says he always kept a side hustle, learned work ethic from his father, and left Banker's Trust in 1985 to play full time while studying with Hillyer and Novak.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: They would always understand, oh Ray needs to go out of town. So I worked at a preschool, a Jewish preschool in Manhattan, and do all my preschool work there, and still do gigs with salsa bands around town and do all of the types of work that I do, and let them know I have to go on a West Coast tour with Mongo, I’ll be out for a month and a half. “No problem Ray, everything’s fine.” So I always worked a side hustle because even when I was working, when I would come off from a month on the road I would always line up tons of salsa work. Because there was so much work to be had. And of course the salsa bands were a great way to generate income. It was also I would do wedding bands, I would do all of this kind of stuff and never like oh I’m above this, I’m a creative — I didn’t talk any of that stuff because I needed to work. But I came up in that kind of generation you know. The working papers in New York State are 14 years old it’s legal. But I came up in a household where like my father would look at me like, “Hey your brother’s twelve years old — when he was twelve years old he was out shining shoes on 149th Street. So it was always a thing of like work to survive. So I always figured out that I needed to keep working. Because before I played music I was doing

private banking at the Banker’s Trust Company of New York and at the time that I was at Banker’s Trust I was still studying with Lonnie Hillyer, studying with Henry Novak, and etcetera, etcetera doing that stuff. And still doing like R&B gigs and salsa gigs. But I hated the job and in 1985 I just left private banking and I started to play music full time. And again my schedule blew up. And I started to work like there was no tomorrow because there was so much work in town. And I wasn’t sitting there going oh man come on now, another salsa gig. I was just like going I have to earn a living.
